steps.title: S1 — count to infinity
steps.body: In DV a node only knows its neighbours' distance claims, so after a link failure bad news spreads slowly and costs can climb step by step (count-to-infinity). In LS every node has the full topology and recomputes correct paths, so the problem does not arise. **S1 true.**

steps.title: S2 and S3 — where shortest paths are computed
steps.body: In LS **every** router runs Dijkstra on its own copy of the link-state database. In DV every router runs the distributed Bellman–Ford update. Neither runs the algorithm at only one node. **S2 false, S3 false.**

steps.title: S4 — message overhead
steps.body: LS floods each router's link-state packet to every router in the network; DV sends one vector only to direct neighbours. So DV needs fewer network messages. **S4 true.**

it-2008-it-69.approach: Walk through the TCP state machine for the passive opener (server) and ask what happens when each handshake segment is lost.

steps.title: Server states (no loss)
steps.body: The server does a passive open → `LISTEN`; on receiving SYN it sends SYN+ACK → `SYN_RCVD`; on receiving the final ACK → `ESTABLISHED`. `SYN_SENT` is the **client's** state after an active open, so **S3 false, S4 true**.

steps.title: Loss of SYN+ACK
steps.body: If SYN+ACK is lost the client never learns the server's ISN and stays in `SYN_SENT`; it cannot send the ACK, so the connection is not established (it must be retried after a timeout). **S1 true.**

steps.title: Loss of the final ACK
steps.body: The client is already `ESTABLISHED` and may send data. Every data segment carries the ACK flag with the same acknowledgement number, so the server moves `SYN_RCVD → ESTABLISHED` on the first data segment (or the server retransmits SYN+ACK and the client re-ACKs). The connection can still be established, so **S2 false**.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: True: S1 and S4 → option **B**.

optionAnalysis.reason: S2 is false (a later ACK-bearing segment completes the handshake) and S3 is false (SYN_SENT is a client state).
